maya: Heads-up — nightly eval (master) shows a sharp regression on the convo prompt set. pass@1 went 94% -> 78% overnight. link: https://internal/evals/1783 (looks correlated with the batching change merged last night) :eyes:

nightly-bot: nightly-eval: job/1783 finished, metric-drop detected: convo.pass1 -16.0 (p<0.01)

jon: ugh. which commit? can you post the commit/brief diff?

maya: commit 9f4b2c3 — changed batching + cache key normalization for prefix cache. I suspect the cache key truncation tweak I made to limit memory is colliding different prefixes. diff snippet below.

maya: ```python
# old: keep raw prefix
def make_key(route_id, prefix_bytes):
    return sha256(route_id + b"::" + prefix_bytes).hexdigest()

# new: normalize + truncate to 64 bytes to reduce KV size
def make_key(route_id, prefix_bytes):
    p = prefix_bytes.lower()[:64]  # <- introduced truncation + lowercasing
    return sha256(p).hexdigest()
```

aditya: ohhh dropping the route_id from the hash is a big red flag — different routes/templates could map to same key now. also lowering might fold case-sensitive tokens.

eva: do we have a repro? I want to see two different prompts producing the same cache hit and then identical output.

maya: yes. quick repro against staging runtime:

maya: ```bash
# prompt A (system+user template A)
curl -s -X POST https://staging.infer/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \n  -d '{"route_id":"conv-a","input":"User: Where is the nearest cafe?"}' > outA.json

# prompt B (different template)
curl -s -X POST https://staging.infer/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \n  -d '{"route_id":"conv-b","input":"user: where is the nearest cafe?"}' > outB.json

# inspect logs (KV cache debug on)
# both requests show: cache_key=0a3f... , cache_hit=true
```

maya: outA and outB are identical (same generation), but they should diverge because conv-a adds context about store hours.

jon: that aligns with the code change (route_id removed and lowercasing). Looks like truncation can make two different prefixes collapse to same 64-byte prefix after lowercase.

aditya: can we run a quick hash-collision scan over our most-used prefixes to estimate collision rate? I can run a small script.

aditya: ```bash
python - <<'PY'
from collections import Counter
pfxs = open('top_prefixes.txt').read().splitlines()
hashes = [hashlib.sha256(p.lower()[:64].encode()).hexdigest() for p in pfxs]
print('unique prefixes', len(pfxs), 'unique hashes', len(set(hashes)))
PY
```

aditya: preliminary run on the top 10k prefixes -> unique prefixes 10000 unique hashes 9987 (13 collisions). that's likely enough to trigger visible regressions in nightly.

eva: thanks. mitigation options? revert the truncation, reintroduce route_id into the key, or namespace by model+route.

maya: I pushed a quick patch to re-add route_id to the key and bumped the prefix size to 128 in a hotfix branch: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/patches/1784 — it passes unit tests locally.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/hotfix/1784 -> staging (canary 1/3).

jon: let's add a targeted eval to nightly that asserts convo.pass1 >= 90 to catch this earlier. Also add a unit test for key uniqueness with real-world prefixes.

aditya: I'll add a small fuzz test to the CI that generates collisions for the current key function and fails on >0 collisions for top-50k prefixes.

maya: note: we should also audit any quantization experiments — similar symptoms can be from quantized kernels being non-deterministic under heavy batching. but logs show cache_hit=true exactly when output is wrong, so cache key bug is primary culprit.

eva: agreed. running the staging canary now with KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 and extra evals. I'll post results in 30m. :thinking_face: 

maya: thanks team. tentative plan: (1) hotfix route_id+larger truncation -> merged to staging (2) add CI fuzz & nightly assertion -> in PR (3) postmortem + checklist for any future optimization that touches key shape/namespace.

jon: assign postmortem to maya+aditya. also ping security if we end up including route identifiers that might contain PII — ensure we salt or use HMAC with a non-exfiltratable secret.

maya: good point — hotfix uses HMAC(route_secret, route_id||prefix) so route_id is not stored raw. patch note included.

nightly-bot: canary job for infra/hotfix/1784 started: job/1784-canary-1

maya: will follow up with concrete numbers from the canary run. thanks :thumbsup:
